P2_fcy_account.answer: Mostly not needed: Monaco uses the euro under a monetary agreement with the EU, having used a predecessor currency (the French franc) before 2002; ordinary local accounts are in euros (European Commission). Accounts in other foreign currencies were not researched.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: No personal income tax for residents (Block3, TaxAtlas); French nationals remain taxable in France. Official position: Monegasque nationals and residents (except French nationals, under the 1963 France–Monaco convention) are not liable for income tax. This applies only to activities carried out by persons genuinely established in Monaco and does not affect other states' rules. TRAP: businesses with an industrial or commercial activity that make more than 25% of their turnover outside Monaco are subject to Business Profit Tax. A sole trader selling mainly to foreign clients may fall in scope; liberal professions may be treated differently (not captured).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Monaco levies VAT on the same basis and at the same rates as France (standard 20%), and the intra-Community regime has applied since 1993. The French VAT rules, including the French small-business franchise thresholds, therefore apply by reference (application to Monaco not separately captured). A free online VAT e-service is available.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
